scope: RB2 logo set only; site, videos, launch kit not yet reviewed

rows.item: concept reads (playhead on a step ruler, one step back)
rows.evidence: Verified: the detached down-pointing marker plus bar now reads as a cursor and the T/pin/1 confusion is gone, and the solid grey fourth tick is clean (no missing-glyph box). But the ticks are fat bars standing on a thick slab, so the set still reads as a bar chart or piano keys, and the wide red bar with a wide triangle above it can read as a necktie or funnel. One step back is carried only by the grey tick sitting to the right of the playhead, which takes explaining.

Contact sheet, true 16 px (light and dark rows): marker, red bar, two ticks, grey tick and rule are all separable, so the separate drawing works and the dark reverse holds. At 16 px the triangle is only about 7 px wide and the left two ticks lose their gap on the light row; favicon-32.png is readable as a red bar with a triangle but looks like a tiny pin or I-beam before it looks like a ruler.

logo-light/dark: Bricolage 800 lowercase, even colour, tight but clean at -0.02 em; no collisions in 'nd' or 'ag'. Weaker points: the g descender and a-g pair are slightly dense, and in the stacked lockup the name is about twice the width of the mark, so the mark feels like an accessory to a large word rather than one lockup.

rows.item: palette fidelity and distinctness from John's other brands
rows.evidence: By eye: warm paper ground, near-black ink, Record red bar, mid grey for the rewound tick, coral on the dark ground; no purple, no navy, no security look. Hex values were not sampled, so fidelity to BRAND.md is judged visually only. Red plus black plus paper is a slightly generic editorial trio, though the dark coral shift is deliberate.

logo-light: block spans y 250 to 795 of 1024 (top gap 250, bottom gap about 229), centred, no clipping; mark and name share the centre axis. Dead margins left and right of the mark are large, and the mark is small against the name. avatar-512: mark spans x 72-440, y 95-417, optically centred and inside a circular crop (rule corner about 217 px from centre, limit 256); the marker sits a little close to the top edge relative to the bottom.

1280x640: clear hierarchy (name about 100 px, two-line tagline, command block, small credit), left edge at 96, right mark ends at 1184, no overlap or clip, mark vertically centred at about y 320. Weak points: the dark command block is the heaviest shape and competes with the mark; the grey credit is low contrast and small; the gap between the text column and the mark is wide so the two halves feel separate.

No gradient, glow, emoji, 3D or mascot; flat geometry only; no purple; the only text claims are the tagline and a real command, and the credit is a plain byline. Nothing presented as AI-generated. The tagline uses 'AI coding agents' as a product descriptor, which is fine.

fixes: Row 1 and 2: thin the ticks and the rule so the mark reads as a measuring ruler rather than a bar chart (ticks about 60 percent of current width, rule about 60 percent of current height) while keeping the playhead bar heavy; re-check at true 16 px that the gaps survive.
Row 1: narrow the marker triangle to roughly the playhead bar width plus one unit each side, and shorten the bar's overhang below the rule, so it stops reading as a necktie or funnel.
Row 1: make 'one step back' legible without explanation, for example give the rewound tick a visibly lower height or a hairline step-gap showing it was the last recorded step, not just a grey colour.
Row 2: in the 16 px drawing keep a 1 px gap between the left tick and the playhead and make the triangle at least 9 px wide; look at the dark row again afterwards.
Row 5: enlarge the mark in logo-light/dark to about 60 to 65 percent of the wordmark width so they read as one lockup; keep the avatar marker 1 unit lower from the top edge.
Row 6: lower the command block's weight (mid-grey fill or outline only) or reduce its width, raise the credit contrast, and bring the mark closer to the text column or enlarge it.
Row 4: sample the exported PNG pixels and paste the hex-to-BRAND.md comparison into the build log so palette fidelity is measured, not eyeballed.
